starting_point: Basic software development, Python or JavaScript, and an understanding of APIs. A prompt-only prototype is a useful first milestone, not the full engineering portfolio.

phase_1.label: Define a bounded assistant
phase_1.slide: One use case, approved documents and a test set
actions: Write ten short fictional workshop FAQs and define what the assistant may and may not answer.
Build a simple interface and define twenty test questions, including missing information and misleading instructions.
phase_1.output: A prototype specification and a labelled evaluation set.

phase_2.label: Connect evidence to answers
phase_2.slide: Retrieve relevant passages and cite the source
actions: Build basic document retrieval, such as local text search, and pass retrieved passages into the answer prompt.
Use a local model if your hardware supports it. Otherwise use a clearly labelled stub and manually evaluated free-chat outputs without pretending the stub is a working model.
phase_2.output: A demonstrable retrieval workflow that separates application code, source text and model responses.

phase_3.label: Measure failure and improve
phase_3.slide: Test unsupported questions, record results and add human review
actions: Score every test answer for source support, correctness and whether the assistant should abstain. Fix one recurring failure.
Document limits, privacy choices and an approval point before any real-world action. Present the result and a realistic next step.
phase_3.output: A small assistant demo plus evaluation results and an honest limitations page.

portfolio: A workshop FAQ assistant that cites its source passages and says when the supplied information is insufficient.
tools: Python, local text search, a small web or command-line interface, and optionally an open local model. Paid APIs are not required.
acceptance: Twenty fixed questions have saved outputs, expected behaviour and human scores.
Every substantive answer cites a supplied source passage, with unsupported claims logged as failures.
Five out-of-scope or missing-information cases trigger abstention or human review, and the README identifies any mocked component.
first_step: Write the assistant's one-sentence purpose and five questions it must decline to answer.
beginner_adjustment: Begin with the workshop's manual prompt workflow while learning Python. Automated agents and fine-tuning are later topics.
